key_insight: Video reasoning can lose touch with what actually appears on screen when it relies only on written reasoning steps. VideoLVR proposes latent visual reasoning grounded in video evidence to address this disconnect.
problem_solved: Language-based reasoning traces do not reliably let multimodal models revisit relevant visual evidence, causing visual forgetting and weakening reasoning about video content.
method: Explore latent visual reasoning grounded in video evidence, as indicated by the paper’s title.
Address limitations of language-only reasoning and symbolic references to visual evidence.
Implementation details and evaluation results are not available in the provided, truncated abstract.
impact: For practitioners, the key takeaway is that stronger video reasoning requires maintaining access to visual evidence—not just generating longer explanations. The excerpt does not establish measured performance gains.

paper_title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
paper_authors: Shilong Li, Xingyuan Bu, Hao Shi, Yun Xing, Weixin Feng
